statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail has risen to 22% and remains below the block threshold, while Stress is high at 65%.
recommendation: Conditions have shifted from a contained overnight range to an observed rates-led downside leg in Nasdaq-100 futures, set against a deepening global bond rout, cycle-high US yields and crude near $87. The identified conditional risk concentration remains the narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC window covering the US cash open and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases. The assessment would move toward the block band only on observed repeated extension after failed retracements.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures break the overnight band to 29,351 as a global bond rout lifts the Japanese 10-year above 3% and the US 10-year to 4.786%
body: NQ futures trade near 29,351.25, about -0.55%, having broken decisively below the 29,434.75-29,570.00 overnight band that had contained trade for the previous several hours. The session range is now 29,327.00-29,571.25 and price sits roughly 20-25 points above the low, so the index is holding in the lower part of its range after a leg of about 220 points. That is a material change from the previous hour, when the band had not extended in either direction. The proximate driver is verified and macro rather than idiosyncratic: Japan's benchmark 10-year government bond yield crossed 3% for the first time since September 1996, with the 5-year at a record 2.265% and the 2-year at a 31-year peak of 1.795%, and the move has propagated across curves. The US 10-year has reached 4.786%, its highest since January 2025, with the 2-year at 4.37%; the German 10-year is near 3.34%, the highest since 2011. Reporting attributes the synchronised selloff to oil-driven inflation pressure, expected central-bank tightening, heavy corporate issuance and fiscal concerns. Energy continues to extend: WTI is near $86.99-87.43 (up roughly 1.4-1.9%) and Brent near $91.51-92.09 after US strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island and Iranian retaliation against bases in Jordan and the UAE. VIX has firmed to 15.39, up 3.15%, trading near its session high of 15.42 but still low in absolute terms. Market pricing for a 25 basis-point September hike stands near 60-65% following Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address. The distinguishing feature of this hour, against the previous ones, is that the cross-asset stack and the index path are now aligned in the same risk-negative direction rather than in conflict, which is a genuine Tail amplifier. What is not yet on record is a sequence: one directional leg has been observed, but no repeated extension after failed retracements and no confirmed shallow-pullback pattern. Tail is therefore raised from 11% to 22%, inside the WATCH band and below the block threshold, Stress is raised to 65% for the deepening bond rout and energy stack, and Confidence is set at 84% on verified current futures levels, yields, crude, volatility and a verified calendar, moderated because the leg is recent and the intra-hour path is known only through level and range rather than tick structure. Delayed shared cross-asset context collected at 05:50 UTC is materially older than the 90-minute freshness bound and predates this move, so it has not been used as evidence for the current price path.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment and every one mapped to the EA_ON band, with Tail between 5 and 17 and Stress rising from 39 to 58. The single Tail peak of 17 came in the 09:00 UTC hour on August 31 during a European event/whipsaw window, and dominant mode was mixed in 22 of the 24 hours. Through the August 31 US session Stress climbed steadily as crude extended on the Larak Island exchange, the 10-year pushed to its highest level since January 2025 and September rate-hike odds firmed after the Jackson Hole address, while Tail stayed compressed between 9 and 13 because the price path itself remained two-sided and mean-reverting. The overnight hours held that pattern with Stress at 50-58 and Tail at 9-11. The break of the overnight band in the current hour is therefore the first directional development in the whole lookback window.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is that today's rates-led leg resolves into two-sided trade rather than into a persistent no-retracement path, so Tail stays inside the WATCH band through the European and early US hours and returns to the EA_ON band from 17:00 UTC. Conditional risk concentrates in the narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open, the final S&P Global Manufacturing PMI and the simultaneous ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases, where forecast Tail peaks at 24 and Stress at 71 with dominant mode projected event/whipsaw, still below the block threshold. Risk is then projected to decay through the US afternoon, with a small power-hour uptick into the 20:00 UTC cash close and a dispersion checkpoint after it as after-hours technology results land. The path reaches its low around 04:00-05:00 UTC before firming modestly with the Tokyo JGB reopen and again into the September 2 European session ahead of ADP. The projection would be invalidated by observed repeated extension after failed retracements, NQ pinning to session lows, a further leg in the global bond rout, or a fresh geopolitical discontinuity in the Strait of Hormuz.
